title: THEY DID AS THE LORD COMMANDED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
Then Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they took the blasphemer outside
the camp and stoned him. The Israelites did as the LORD commanded Moses
- Lev 24:23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends soberly. What God commanded was carried out. The closing
line is simple: the Israelites did as the LORD commanded Moses.

We should not pretend this is a comfortable verse. It is not. A man died.
And yet the narrator's note is telling — Israel, so often disobedient in
these wilderness chapters, here did exactly what God said.

There are two things to carry away, and we need both.

First, God is not casual about sin. We live in a time that finds this
difficult, preferring a God who is endlessly tolerant. Scripture will not
give us that God. Paul writes that the wages of sin is death (Rom 6:23).
Hebrews reminds us our God is a consuming fire (Heb 12:29).

Second, and this is the heart of the matter, look at what God has done
with that justice. Paul writes that God presented Christ as a sacrifice
of atonement, so that He might be just and the one who justifies those
who have faith in Jesus (Rom 3:25-26). God did not lower His standard.
He absorbed its cost Himself.

The lamps burned continually. The bread sat continually. And now Christ
lives continually to intercede for us (Heb 7:25). The judgment of
Leviticus 24 and the mercy of Calvary meet at one cross.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I hold together both God's justice and His mercy?
2. Have I truly reckoned with what my sin cost Christ?
3. What does obedience to God look like for me today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Holy and merciful God, thank You that You did not set aside justice but
satisfied it Yourself in Jesus. Give me a heart that fears You rightly
and rests in Your grace completely. Amen.
